# WH-003 Short/Over/Damaged (OS&D) Policy

## 1. Purpose

### 1.1 Objective
This policy defines what the dock team does when a delivery is short, over or damaged, so that Meridian Supply Co. preserves its right to recover cost from the carrier or supplier.

### 1.2 Definitions
- Short: fewer units received than shown on the ASN or packing slip.
- Over: more units received than ordered.
- Damaged: units or packaging with visible or concealed damage on receipt.

## 2. Exceptions at the Dock

### 2.1 Note the exception on the bill of lading
Before signing the carrier's bill of lading, the receiver writes the exception on it, for example "2 cartons crushed" or "short 40 units". A clean signature on a delivery with an exception weakens any later claim. The driver countersigns the note where possible.

### 2.2 Photograph
The receiver photographs the damaged packaging, the damaged goods, the trailer condition and the labels. Photos are attached to the receiving record before the carrier leaves or, for concealed damage, as soon as it is found.

### 2.3 Notify Procurement within 24 hours
Procurement is notified of every OS&D exception within 24 hours of receipt. The notice contains the PO number, supplier, item, quantity affected and the photos. Procurement then agrees the remedy with the supplier.

## 3. Overages

### 3.1 Overage threshold
An overage up to and including 5% of the ordered quantity may be received at the buyer's discretion. Overages above 5% are held, not received into stock, until the buyer decides whether to accept or return the excess.

### 3.2 Hold location
Held overages stay in the marked OS&D hold lane and are labelled with the PO number and the date held.

## 4. Shortages

### 4.1 Short shipments
A short shipment is received for the quantity actually counted. The balance remains open on the PO. Procurement decides whether to wait for a back-order, cancel the balance or source elsewhere.

## 5. Damaged Goods

### 5.1 Quarantine
Damaged goods are quarantined in the OS&D lane and are not put away to stock. The Quality team inspects the goods and decides on disposition: return to supplier, scrap or use as is with a documented concession.

### 5.2 Link to supplier quality
Where damage is attributable to supplier packaging rather than the carrier, Quality is informed so that a nonconformance report can be raised under QA-001.

## 6. Claims

### 6.1 Carrier claim within 30 days
A claim against the carrier must be filed within 30 days of the delivery date. Procurement files the claim using the photos, the annotated bill of lading and the receiving record. Claims not filed within 30 days are not pursued.

### 6.2 Summary of deadlines

| Step | Deadline |
|---|---|
| Note exception on bill of lading | Before signing |
| Notify Procurement | Within 24 hours |
| Carrier claim | Within 30 days |

## 7. Records

### 7.1 Exception log
Each exception is logged with its reference, outcome and the credit or replacement received. The log is reviewed monthly.

### 7.2 Responsibilities
The receiver notes, photographs and logs the exception. The Warehouse Supervisor checks that the bill of lading note and photos are in place before the carrier leaves. Procurement agrees the remedy and files the carrier claim. Quality decides the disposition of damaged goods.

### 7.3 Concealed damage
Damage found after the carrier has left is reported to Procurement as soon as it is found, with photographs of the goods and packaging, so that the carrier can be told within the claim period.
